record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study conceptually tests whether capacity pressure can lead a model to consolidate feature information around designated representations, using fine-tuning and linear probes rather than the original toy-model method. It does not test sparse-feature superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports that trained flags classify features and that forcibly clamping them steers generation. Those results concern installed, deliberately trained control flags, not spontaneous superposition or polysemanticity. The probe and perplexity results are retained as evidence about feature consolidation and representational capacity. No results cited from other work are included.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Phi-3-Mini to write trained flags into 16 reserved dimensions, so the feature structure is induced on purpose. It then measures how much feature information stays in the other dimensions, the perplexity cost, and steering. It never measures superposition, polysemantic neurons, feature geometry, or SAE features arising on their own. The capacity-pressure account is the authors' interpretation, not a test of V2. V2 concerns why naturally polysemantic neurons share capacity, which is a different construct from erosion of redundant copies of installed flags. Superposition is mentioned only in the introduction as background. None of the versions is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a feature reliably supplied at a fixed location becomes an authoritative internal feature. The model erodes its redundant encodings, so the flags work as control switches. They attribute this to efficiency pressure under finite capacity. The capacity attribution is argued rather than directly tested: no experiment varies capacity, and the perplexity table measures only the cost of fencing.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes a 3.8B LLM with 16 designated residual-stream dimensions, synthetic feature labels, and an auxiliary position loss. It does not reproduce toy-network sparse-feature superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of fenced dimensions changes the reported perplexity cost. Feature-specific probe drops vary; the probe comparison is reported at layer k=10. The text also says flags are less clean in layers k < 5 than from layer 5 onward.

fits_no_version.finding: After fine-tuning with flags injected and then a position loss, linear probes on the non-fenced dimensions recover the fenced features less well than probes on the full baseline model (average 82.3 to 71.9). An unfenced control feature changes little (87.0 to 85.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: When a feature is reliably supplied at fixed residual dimensions during fine-tuning, an LLM reduces redundant encodings of it elsewhere.

fits_no_version.finding: Reserving more residual dimensions for flags raises WikiText-2 perplexity: 11.04 at 0, 11.16 at 16, 12.04 at 64 and 12.22 at 128 dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Commandeering residual-stream dimensions for installed features carries a perplexity cost that grows with the number of dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: Clamping the installed flags at inference steers story content, even when the flags contradict the prompt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained residual-stream flags become causal control points for generation.

record.problems: Evidence is from one model and manually installed features trained on synthetic data. The probe comparison is reported at a single layer, and the paper gives no error bars or significance tests. The forced-generation demonstrations are qualitative and deliberately induced.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy model, sparse features, near-orthogonal overlapping directions, sparsity transition, or geometry.
All parts: no measurement of whether natural polysemantic neurons arise from capacity competition, or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
All parts: no study of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
All parts: does not measure the distribution of natural features across neurons or recover features with an SAE.
All parts: no SAE features examined.
All parts: does not examine the dimensionality of naturally represented features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V2 'supports' labels are dropped. The behaviour is deliberately installed via an auxiliary loss, and none of the measures target polysemanticity, superposition geometry or SAE features. The probe comparison is also confounded: it pits different models against different dimension sets. It is reported at one layer (k=10) with no error bars. One model only (Phi-3-Mini). Preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test naturally occurring sparse features, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry.

Tests capacity-related consolidation for manually installed features in one LLM, but not whether naturally polysemantic neurons arise from competition, whether important features get dedicated neurons or dimensions, or whether other features share them.
Does not investigate alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity occurs without capacity pressure.
Does not measure whether naturally occurring LLM features are distributed across many neurons or recoverable with an SAE.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not determine whether naturally represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relation.reason: Superposition and polysemanticity motivate the introduction, but the experiments concern deliberately installed representations.

tranche.reason: The study induces feature flags and measures steering, probe recoverability and perplexity costs. It neither tests a listed superposition version nor uses superposition as its method.

source_check.notes: Probe comparisons use 3072 baseline dimensions versus 3056 non-fenced dimensions after training. The capacity explanation is argued; fencing width varies, but model capacity is not independently manipulated.
